author: IGN
description:
EA Sports NHL 27 reviewed by Marc Deschamps on Xbox Series X|S, also available on PlayStation 5.

"Hockey is one of the greatest sports in the world, and NHL 27 remains enjoyable largely due to that simple fact. The satisfaction of delivering a bone-crushing hit or snapping a wrist shot past a goaltender is just as effective as ever, and tiny tweaks to stuff like stadiums and music continue to add authenticity in small doses – but there are no illusions that anything truly substantial has changed this year. With franchises like NHL Hitz and NHL 2K long dead, there really aren’t any other options on the market. This lack of competition puts the hockey faithful in a difficult position, and doubly so since there weren’t many changes in NHL 26 compared to NHL 25 to begin with. The handful of differences here are mostly welcome, nothing is worse than last year, but very little is better either. It’s a shame that NHL 27 is still stuck in the past."

#IGN #Gaming
title: NHL 27 Review

The skill trees in The Blood of Dawnwalker go way beyond the standard "get a point, buy a skill" system. Between managing valuable in-game time, hunting down specific skill manuals in the world, and raising your corruption levels by drinking blood, building out Coen's arsenal takes some strategy. In this video, we break down exactly how the Witchcraft, Swordmastery, and Vampirism trees work, how to equip your abilities, and give our top recommendations on the absolute best early skills to grab first.

Whether you prefer wielding a sword in the daylight or unleashing Coen's Vrakhiri vampire claws at night, optimizing your build early on is crucial. We dive into essential early-game abilities like Haste, Soul Reaping, Charge, and Voracious Bite, alongside vital perks that boost your armor, stamina, and activation charges. Knowing how to balance your weapon types and manage your health costs will give you a massive advantage against both standard enemies and tough bosses.

author: IGN
description:
Open-world games. Arguably, no other genre has defined modern gaming more than the expansive, experimental, and exciting places this genre has taken us to. Over the past 30 years, we’ve gone from grey, empty streets begging to be torn up in a blocky muscle car to glorious, colourful fantasy lands full of adventure and opportunity. But what are the games that have stood out the most, pushed the form forward, and ultimately led to GTA 6’s moment? 

As part of IGN 30, I’m going to try to answer that question by walking you through five distinct flavours of open-world game before deciding on the greatest of them all. From web-swinging superheroes and sword-swinging monster hunters to bank heists and shrine raids, here are the 30 masterpieces of open-world game design.
